title: Deny-by-Default Permission Engine
scope: Map OpenWorker's RiskClass + Mode permission system that prevents hallucinated destructive tool calls from executing without approval.

risk_classes.read: RiskClass.READ — no side effects, always allowed
risk_classes.external: RiskClass.EXTERNAL — side effects off-machine (connector sends), unattended Inbox hook

modes.discuss: Mode.DISCUSS — read-only conversation, no edits/planning workflow
modes.plan: Mode.PLAN — read-only + planning contract (explore → propose_plan → execute)
modes.interactive: Mode.INTERACTIVE — ask for approval (default), auto-allow reads
modes.custom: Mode.CUSTOM — interactive + auto-allow the config's auto_allow tools

classification.priority: user-local override → by-name base table (WRITE_TOOLS, SHELL_TOOL) → aisuite metadata.requires_approval → READ fallback
classification.base_table: WRITE_TOOLS = {write_file, replace_in_file, apply_patch, apply_unified_diff}, SHELL_TOOL = run_shell
classification.consequence_check: is_consequential(risk) returns True for anything != READ — drives permission gating

decision_model.dataclass: Decision(allowed: bool, reason: str, needs_user: bool, rule: str)
decision_model.needs_user: True → surface prompts user for approval before executing
decision_model.standing_rules: standing_rule_candidate() returns target value for task-scoped 'allow this path' rules (§25 invariant)

authorization_flow.step3: If allowed and decision.rule is set → audit auto_allowed
authorization_flow.step4: If denied and needs_user → emit PERMISSION_REQUIRED event, await approver
authorization_flow.step5: If denied → append _tool_error_message to history (no orphans)

guard_toolset_integration.class: GuardToolset (factory/infra/tools_guard.py:100) — WrapperToolset that confines all worker tools
guard_toolset_integration.current_gates: senior-role deny check at line 155-156; mandatory-planning gate at line 157-161 (blocks _MODIFY_TOOLS until 'remember' called); unknown/discovery tool warning at lines 176-179
guard_toolset_integration.gap: No RiskClass classification gate — all modification tools in _MODIFY_TOOLS (replace_text, write_file, replace_function, etc.) execute directly once _has_planned is True (lines 167-168). No per-tool risk evaluation, no Mode-based approval, no _tool_error_message feedback path for denied/unknown-risk calls. A hallucinated destructive call (wrong file path / dangerous command) executes without any permission check.
guard_toolset_integration.deny_by_default_risk_gate: Should be inserted in call_tool between the senior-role block (line 156) and the modify-tools gate (line 157): classify each tool by RiskClass, default to INTERACTIVE mode (ask on writes/exec), and raise PermissionDenied for denied calls so the LLM learns the constraint in-turn.

proposal: ai-factory's tools_guard.py allows ALL tools by default — there is no deny-by-default gate. When the LLM hallucinates a destructive tool call (e.g. editing the wrong file, running a dangerous command), it executes without any permission check. OpenWorker's RiskClass + Mode system ensures only READ tools auto-pass; WRITE_LOCAL and EXEC require explicit approval or standing rules. ai-factory should adopt a similar classification: classify each shadow tool by risk (read/write/shell), default to INTERACTIVE mode (ask on writes/shell), and append _tool_error_message for denied calls so the LLM learns what it can't do.

pydantic_ai_2_impl.pattern: Risk-aware tool-error feedback: classify each tool by RiskClass at the call_tool boundary; reject non-READ calls in INTERACTIVE mode by raising a PermissionDenied exception whose message is surfaced to the LLM as a tool-error result (no silent execution); the LLM self-corrects in-turn. Integrated into GuardToolset.call_tool (tools_guard.py:152) so the gate fires before any _MODIFY_TOOLS invocation.
pydantic_ai_2_impl.why_now: ai-factory's LLMs execute destructive edits without any gate — a hallucinated file path causes real damage before any verification runs. OpenWorker's deny-by-default + tool-error feedback (engine.py:757-766) prevents this: denied calls get a visible error message in history, and the LLM learns the constraint in-turn. GuardToolset.call_tool (tools_guard.py:152) already intercepts all tool calls and has a mandatory-planning gate (line 157) but no RiskClass classification — adding classify() + _authorize() before line 167 would close the gap with zero architectural disruption.
pydantic_ai_2_impl.harness_gap: factory/infra/tools_guard.py:152 — GuardToolset.call_tool has no RiskClass classification gate. The senior-role deny check (lines 155-156) and mandatory-planning gate (lines 157-161) are the only pre-execution filters; after _has_planned is True, all _MODIFY_TOOLS (replace_text, write_file, replace_function, add_import, add_constant, move_symbol, delete_file, rename_file — defined at line 97) execute directly at lines 167-168 with no per-tool risk evaluation. No Mode enum, no RiskClass classification, no PermissionDenied/_tool_error_message feedback path for denied calls. A hallucinated destructive tool call (wrong file path, dangerous command) executes without any permission check. Insert classify() + _authorize() between the senior-role block (line 156) and the modify-tools gate (line 157), raising PermissionDenied (surfaced as tool-error) for non-READ tools in INTERACTIVE mode.
